hens_rule_text: up to 6 chickens on lots under 10,000 sq ft, 12 on lots 10,000 to 20,000 sq ft, 24 on lots over 20,000 sq ft
permit_notes: A $25 urban agriculture animal-keeping permit is required.
setback_notes: Enclosures must be set back at least 10 ft from all property lines (not stated as distance from a home specifically); roosters must be kept at least 50 ft from all property lines.
coop_rules: Enclosures must provide at least 4 sq ft per adult bird and be set back at least 10 ft from property lines; birds must be kept secured and not allowed to run at large.
zoning_notes: Rules are set citywide in the Zoning Code, Chapter 1422 (Urban Agriculture, Animal Keeping), which also covers ducks, quail, doves, rabbits, bees, turkeys and goats.
hoa_note: Homeowners associations, deed restrictions and leases can be stricter than city law. Check yours before getting chickens.

sources.name: Cincinnati Zoning Code Chapter 1422, Sec. 1422-05 Domestic Residence keeping (Municode)
Cincinnati Magazine, Local Laws for Homesteading
CoopCraft Guide, Cincinnati Ohio Chicken Laws

research_notes: Two independent search queries returned matching search-result extracts citing the same Municode Chapter 1422 section (lot-size tiered hen limits, rooster ratio and setback, permit fee, coop density), which agree with each other and with a local magazine's coverage; the full code text was not opened directly, so treated as a search-extract read.
